page: Amazon Web Services x2iedn.16xlarge is a memory-optimized instance powered by the AWS Nitro System. It features 64 vCPUs and 32 physical cores driven by an Intel Xeon 8375C processor running at 3.5 GHz. The system is equipped with 2048 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, yielding an exceptionally high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 32 GB per vCPU. Local storage is provided via a 1900 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance supports a baseline network bandwidth of 50 Gbps.

Benchmark results indicate strong multi-core processing capabilities, with a stress-ng multi-core CPU score of 61947.26 and a PassMark CPU score of 56826.42. The instance excels in database operations, scoring in the top tier of PassMark database benchmarks with 26144.88. Memory bandwidth tests show average performance, reaching 153.34 GB/sec for large block reads and 61.06 GB/sec for large block writes. Single-core performance remains average, as shown by a Geekbench single-core score of 1688.0.

From a resource density perspective, this instance offers high qualitative cost efficiency for memory-bound workloads due to its massive DDR4 memory allocation relative to compute cores. However, because it lacks GPU acceleration, it is not suited for heavy parallel graphics processing or massive-scale AI training, though it demonstrates strong text generation speeds for small and medium LLM inference.

The x2iedn.16xlarge is designed for memory-intensive enterprise workloads. It is highly suitable for large-scale in-memory databases, high-performance database operations, software compilation, and memory-heavy data processing pipelines.
